## v1.8, or: the last time you'll download this by hand. Probably.

Every release has ended the same way: download a zip, unzip it, drag it somewhere, recite an `xattr` spell at macOS, click "Run anyway" at SmartScreen. This release ends that, starting with the next one. You still have to download this one by hand, because v1.7.1 doesn't know how to update itself. Think of it as the last stamp on the punch card.

Your saves, settings, rumble, MSU pack and CRT obsession all carry over, as always.

### The game updates itself

When the start menu opens, it quietly asks GitHub whether there's anything newer. It does that in the background, so the window never waits on the network. If there is something newer, an **UPDATE TO V1.9** button (or whatever's newest) shows up right under the title. Press it, say yes, watch the bar fill, and the game replaces itself and starts the new version. Nothing downloads until you press the button.

- **Mac:** the whole `ALTTP-DX.app` is swapped for the new one. A file the game downloads itself isn't quarantined, so the `xattr` step is gone for good after this release.
- **Linux:** the AppImage is replaced in place, under the same filename, so your shortcuts keep working. The filename will keep saying the version you first downloaded. It's lying, but it's lying helpfully.
- **Windows:** the files next to `zelda3.exe` are replaced, all except `zelda3.ini`, which is yours. Windows won't overwrite a program that's running, so the old files are set aside and tidied up the next time the game starts.

Every download is checked against the size and SHA-256 that GitHub publishes for it before anything gets replaced. If something goes wrong (no internet, a folder the game isn't allowed to write to), it says what happened and offers to open the release page so you can grab it yourself.

### Two new settings

Under **General**:

- **Check For Updates**, on by default. Turn it off and the game never phones home.
- **Update Channel**: **Releases** for the numbered releases, or **Nightly** for the rolling test build of whatever's newest. Nightly is rebuilt most nights and is sometimes broken, so pick it knowing that. Switch back to Releases and the next real release is your next update.

### Which version am I on?

The start menu says so now, in the bottom-right corner: `V1.8`, `NIGHTLY` and its commit, or `DEV BUILD` if you built it yourself. A build you made yourself never offers to update, because replacing your work in progress with a zip off the internet would be rude.

### Smaller things

- The updater only replaces the game. The tools (`zelda3-tools`) are still a download of their own.
- It only checks when the start menu opens. If you've turned the start menu off, nothing gets checked.
- For terminal people: `--version` prints the version, `--check-update releases` asks GitHub without changing anything, and `--update releases` (or `nightly`) does the whole update from the command line.

### Getting it running

1. Download the game for your system, and the tools if you want them.
2. **macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 11+):** unzip and drag `ALTTP-DX.app` to Applications, then run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/ALTTP-DX.app` (and the same for `zelda3-tools.app`) once. That's the last time for the game, I promise. Updates need permission to write where the app lives, which an admin account has in Applications.
3. **Linux (x86_64, glibc 2.35+):** `chmod +x` the AppImage and run it. Keep it somewhere you can write to, like `~/Applications`, so it can update itself. If it complains about FUSE, install `libfuse2` or `fuse3`, or add `--appimage-extract-and-run`.
4. **Windows (x86_64):** unzip anywhere you can write to and run `zelda3.exe` or `zelda3-tools.exe`. SmartScreen will still clutch its pearls: "More info", then "Run anyway". Updates don't ask again.
5. Give the game your US ROM and press Play. For randomizer seeds, generate one on alttpr.com from the Japanese 1.0 ROM (MD5 `03a63945398191337e896e5771f77173`) and drop it on the Randomizer page. No game data is included, as ever.
